floor_history.headline: Recon: whole residual localized to ONE register-allocation decision (offset allocno takes $a1, forcing the $a2/$a3 swap + a failed-coalesce 'move $a1,$a3'); operand-order axis eliminated at flat floor

frontier.hypothesis: The 'offset' allocno is given $a1 for a knowable reason — either allocno-priority ordering (reg_n_refs / live length) or an explicit copy preference — and the .greg dump names which, selecting the lever.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 global.c allocno assignment: local-alloc places block-local quantities first, then global-alloc walks allocnos in priority order honouring expand_preferences copy hints; the ';; Register dispositions:' section plus the conflict lists state the outcome and the conflicts directly.
frontier.next_probe: Run the mandated Step-0 diagnosis from .claude/rules/register-alloc-pure-c.md: reproduce the cpp invocation from engine/buildconfig.py to get a preprocessed main.i (the sandbox does not keep one), then 'cc1 <build flags> -da main.i' and read the register dispositions and conflicts for the offset and base_ptr allocnos. Has never been run on this function.

frontier.hypothesis: Keeping the $a1 parameter live deeper into the entry block forces the 'offset' allocno onto $a2 (target's assignment) and simultaneously removes the join copy, closing both halves of the residual at once.
frontier.mechanism: Target performs 'move $s1,$a1' AFTER 'lw $v1,0($a3)'; ours performs it before the whole entry chain, retiring $a1 early. If $a1 is still occupied when global-alloc reaches the offset allocno it must take $a2 — which is exactly target's assignment and needs no copy.
frontier.next_probe: Try C forms that delay the last use of the a1 parameter past the table load: order the base_ptr/base statements so the table 'lw' precedes the *0xB0 chain's read of a1, or derive offset from a later read of the parameter. Measure with diffit.py and watch specifically for 'move $s1,$a1' moving after 'lw $v1,0(...)' and the disappearance of 'move $a1,$a3'.

frontier.hypothesis: Changing the ARITHMETIC of the *0xB0 chain (not merely naming an intermediate, which H4 killed) changes which insn defines the value crossing the entry-block boundary, letting it coalesce with the offset allocno.
frontier.mechanism: The copy exists because the chain's final 'sll ,4' writes a block-local quantity assigned by local-alloc before global-alloc runs. A re-association whose final operation is not that shift changes the definition point of the cross-block value.
frontier.next_probe: Measure re-associated forms such as 'offset = (s16)a1 * 0x10 * 0xB' and '(s16)a1 * 0xB * 0x10' with diffit.py (NOT the scalar score), checking whether the multiply chain's last insn writes the register that the +0x98 sites subsequently read.
